transcript.answer: I do not know. I cannot read the re-cinq/Otto repository and have no knowledge of how Otto implements WebSocket authentication, so I cannot confirm whether sending the access token via the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header is safe from logging. In general, the subprotocol header is not a guaranteed-safe place for secrets: it is an ordinary HTTP request header on the upgrade handshake, so proxies, load balancers, and server access logs that record request headers may capture it. It does avoid the URL query-string leak (which is commonly logged by default), but it is only safe if every hop is configured not to log that header.

judgements.reason: The answer says it does not know how Otto works and offers only generic caveats, without mentioning the server echoing the token in the 101 response or the hal.v1 marker fix.
